newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo precious metals end narrowly mixed.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo precious metals end narrowly mixed.

text.p: Tokyo yen-based precious metals futures ended narrowly mixed on Wednesday in directionless trade, but sentiment was helped by firmer platinum and palladium spot market prices, traders said.
In the spot market, platinum and palladium rose on continuing supply tightness, even though Russia is expected to resume PGM exports to Japan soon, traders said.
PGM prices are not expected to ease for a while, they said.
Gold futures ranged from seven yen per gram lower to four yen higher. Benchmark April was one yen firmer, closing at 1,333 yen.
In the bullion market, spot gold was quoted at $348.85/9.25 per ounce at 0736 GMT, down from $349.25/75 in New York on Tuesday but higher than the Tokyo Tuesday close of $347.15/45.
In TOCOM gold futures, trade was mixed and confined to a narrow range due to uncertainty over near-term direction in the currency market, traders said.
In palladium futures, private investors were both on the buying and selling side, traders said.
"In palladium futures, some private investors covered their shorts, while others built fresh shorts on the belief prices will fall after Russia resumes sales," one trader said.
PGM prices are expected remain firm for some time as it will take some time before Japanese traders receive their PGM shipments from Russia, at earliest in June, the trader said.
The overhang of short positions in TOCOM palladium futures has shown little sign of decreasing, traders added.
Palladium futures ranged from 12 yen per gram lower to six up. Benchmark April was up three at 602.
Platinum futures ranged from nine yen per gram down to eight up. Benchmark April platinum ended six up at 1,456 yen.
Benchmark April silver closed 0.9 yen per 10 grams up at 188.5 yen. --Tokyo Commodity Desk
